title: Callback and Microtask Queues Check
description: Compare Promise microtasks vs setTimeout tasks.

questions.explanation: After sync (`start`, `end`), the microtask queue drains before the next timer task.

questions.prompt:
For chained microtasks:

```js
Promise.resolve()
  .then(() => console.log("m1"))
  .then(() => console.log("m2"));
setTimeout(() => console.log("t1"), 0);
```

What is the order?
questions.explanation: The microtask queue is drained completely — so both `m1` and `m2` run before task `t1`.

options.text: Schedule `fn` as a task after current sync work and after microtasks drain
Run `fn` on a background thread for 0 ms

questions.explanation: Delay `0` still queues a macrotask. It runs after the current sync pass and after the microtask queue is empty.

options.text: Idle callbacks with lower priority than timers

questions.explanation: Promise reactions are microtasks. That is why they usually run before `setTimeout(..., 0)` callbacks.
